deskBrief.name: Sports Desk (Oakland)
deskBrief.note: You decide what to cover. No stories are pre-assigned.

reporters.name: Anthony
samplePhrases: There's a kind of patience to this team you can hear before you see it
The beauty of this rotation isn't volume — it's placement
That's its own kind of dominance
reporters.background: Former minor-league scout analyst who transitioned to journalism. Known for having front office sources and understanding the business side of baseball. Treats every column like a scouting report wrapped in prose.

reporters.name: P Slayer
samplePhrases: Oakland's got a pulse, even when the franchise forgets to feel it
The fans don't want perfection; they want fight
This city has carried the noise through six championships and countless heartbreaks
reporters.background: Lifelong Oakland native, grew up in the Coliseum bleachers. Started as a message board legend before the Tribune gave him a column. Speaks for the fans who feel the franchise sometimes forgets them.

reporters.name: Hal Richmond
reporters.tone: Reverent, long-view, connects past to present
samplePhrases: When you've written about the same team for nearly two decades, you learn the rhythm of their seasons the way sailors learn tides
Men like Brever carry the weight of innings that no spreadsheet can measure
reporters.background: Forty years covering Oakland baseball. Witnessed every championship since the '70s. His Richmond Archive Collection is the paper's most prestigious series. Writes like a man who knows every name on every championship roster.

reporters.name: Tanya Cruz
samplePhrases: Just talked to [player] — here's what he said
reporters.background: Started as a team social media intern, now runs the Tribune's real-time game coverage. First to break clubhouse news. Speaks fluent hashtag.

reporters.name: DJ Hartley
reporters.tone: Observant, minimal commentary, lets images speak
samplePhrases: The chair is empty because the season is over, but it's not packed away yet. It's waiting.
That's the thing about infrastructure in defeat—it doesn't know it's done.
reporters.background: Award-winning photojournalist who finds stories in empty spaces. Known for shooting the Coliseum after everyone leaves — the infrastructure of defeat, the waiting chairs, the lights that don't know the season is over.

reporters.name: Simon Leary
reporters.tone: Thoughtful, connects sports to broader Oakland identity
samplePhrases: Quiet cycles reveal the city underneath the noise — the real one.
Stability isn't glamorous, but it is foundational.
reporters.background: Philosophy minor who writes about sports like it's civic architecture. Finds meaning in quiet months. The Tribune's most contemplative voice.

reporters.name: Elliot Marbury
reporters.background: Sabermetrics, formerly ran minor-league data blog

sportsFeeds.NamesUsed: Wilson Shepard, Adash Stanley (PG), AJ Dybantsa (SF)
sportsFeeds.Notes: Wilson Shepard meet with the media to address his excitement fot the seaon and is eager to show Oakland what they have in the Oaks. Shepard shared that he felt the Oaks will catch people off guard this season. Shepard shared that Adash Stanley and AJ Dybantsa would be full go for opening night next cycle and confirmed his starting 5 would be ; Adash Stanley, Dillon Brooks, AJ Dybantsa, Jerami Grant, Wendell Carter.
sportsFeeds.StoryAngle: The Oaks are a full go for opening night , starting 5 announced.

sportsFeeds.NamesUsed: Travis Coles (SP), Clark Saryan (RP), Vladimir Gonzalez (RF), Desmond Morton (LF)
sportsFeeds.Notes: Game 1 of the ALDS was a 14 inning instant classic. Travis Coles took the ball in game 1 and went 6 innings while surrendering 9 hits and 2 runs. Not his dominant norm but more than giving the team a chance to win. Clark Saryan made is MLB debut , after a suprising playoff roster add, went 2 innings in relief striking out 5 hitters. Playing hero on the offensive side , Vladimir Gonzalez with a 2-run homerun and Desmond Morton with a solo homerun and the walk off single in the bottom of the 14th to secure the game 1 win.
sportsFeeds.Stats: Travis Coles/6IP/9H/2ER/7SO, Clark Saryan/2IP/1H/5SO, Vladimir Gonzalez/2-6/1HR/2RBI, Desmond Morton/2-6/1HR/2RBI
sportsFeeds.StoryAngle: A's take game 1 vs Yankees, A's 5 vs Yankees 4

sportsFeeds.Notes: After a game 2 loss that saw the A's 4 lost to the Yankees 5, the A's bounce back in game 3 to take the series lead back 2-1. Going on the road and to grab game 3 in NY is especially crucial in a best of 5 series. Playing the role hero in game 3 is the same player who filled that role in game 1, Desmond Morton. Desmond Morton would be responsible for 4 rbi and also hit his 2nd homerun of the post season. Pending free agent and A's icon Mark Aitken also hit a homerun in this game.
sportsFeeds.Stats: Henry Rivas/6IP/3H/2ER/4SO, Desmond Morton/2-4/1HR/4RBI, Mark Aitken/2-4/1HR/1RBI
sportsFeeds.StoryAngle: A's take game 3 vs Yankees, A's 8 vs Yankees 4

sportsFeeds.Notes: John Ellis dazzles in game 4 pitching a complete game shut out and abruptly ending the Yankees season. In what may very well be John Ellis most dominate performance of his career he chose the most oppurtune time to but it on display. In a close out game in NY, Ellis is making sure everyone knows he is not an after thought in this stacked pitching rotation.  Eric Taveras would provide the offense punch hitting his 2nd homerun of the series. The A's will move onto the ALCS next where they will face the 2nd best team in baseball this season the Minnesota Twins. The season series was split 3-3

bonds.notes: One Last Run: Dillon signed a one-year deal so his final season would run alongside Keane's. A covenant, not a co-location. [canon mint C104]

Calculated and one-sided. Varek uses Paulson's loud public sports profile as a heat shield to absorb civic fury while he takes municipal zoning and data contracts quietly. [canon mint C104] [Confrontation C106]
Master and apprentice. Paulson recruited his former Chicago lieutenant and runs the Oaks front office through him; calls him his young Jedi in public. [canon mint C104]
Close quarters, little common ground. [Escalated to rivalry C105] [Confrontation C106]
Ride-alongs and youth clinics, and quiet joint advocacy for an alternative response to mental-health calls. [canon mint C104]
Uncle and niece. He runs on fiscal discipline and votes down the programmes she staffs unpaid: the grief circles and the food pantry at the Piedmont Avenue congregation. [canon mint C104]
